notes: Documentation only (JSON has no comments); not part of the rules. Design: docs/design/catalog-and-approval.md (skill package policy section) and the skill package policy row in docs/design/decisions.md.

Regexes are RE2 / ECMAScript-compatible. In JavaScript compile them with the 'g' flag only (not 'u' or 'v': [^}] and the trailing '-' do not compile under 'v') and delete matches with replace(re, '') -- Go uses ReplaceAllLiteralString(line, "").

Measured executing on Claude Code (with negative controls): !` inline, fenced, indented and inside HTML comments; !$ARGUMENTS`x` and arguments [who] + !$who`x` with no arguments; ```$ARGUMENTS! with no arguments; !$ARGUMENTS with an argument starting with a backtick; arguments [ARGUMENTSx] / [1a] / [a.b] with ``$name`! (2.1.295, no arguments).

Defensive, no execution evidence: fence then $ (```$ARGUMENTS called with an argument '!' did not execute; it guards arguments starting with ! or a backtick); !$0`x`; !${...}`x`. fence-then-$ may over-reject normal docs that put a $variable right after a fence on the same line; !$ rejects text like 'costs !$5' or 'wow!$HOME'.

arguments names: argument_name_pattern plus no argument_name_forbidden_prefixes entry as a prefix, compared ASCII case-insensitively (conservative: Claude Code's $ARGUMENTS replacement is case-sensitive). Only empty, [a, b] (same line) or space/tab-separated plain names on the same line, or a block list of '- name' lines with one indentation; anything else (quotes, mappings, comments, block scalars) is skill_md_invalid.

package.forbidden_path_segments: any path in the package (file or directory, any depth) with a segment equal to one of these under Unicode simple case folding (Go strings.EqualFold; conservative) is PACKAGE_UNSAFE forbidden_path, checked before everything else; vectors expect result forbidden_path with the first such file in path byte order. Claude Code 2.1.295 does not load a nested .claude/ inside an installed skill (measured); this is defense in depth.

Placeholder deletion, both ways, either hit rejects: (1) delete placeholder_sigil + each declared name (union over every SKILL.md in the package, longest first, literal), check; then delete builtin_placeholder_patterns in order, check; (2) delete placeholder_pattern repeatedly until the line stops changing, check. The raw line and the !$ substring are checked first.

version: allowed at most once (a duplicate is SKILL_FRONTMATTER_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED like any other key). Its format (SemVer 2.0.0 without a leading v or build metadata, at most 64 bytes, a scalar on the key's line) is not part of this policy: the publisher checks it when parsing the root SKILL.md (PACKAGE_UNSAFE skill_md_invalid), and whether it is greater than the skill's existing versions is the publisher's version rule (SKILL_VERSION_INVALID).
